text: What has keys but opens no locks, and has hammers inside?
explain: A piano has keys you press, and little hammers strike its strings.

text: What has hands, tells the time, but cannot clap?
explain: A clock has hands that point to the time, but they cannot clap.

text: What gets wetter the more it dries?
explain: A towel dries you, so the more it dries, the wetter it gets.

text: You twist off its cap and pour from its neck, yet it has no head. What is it?
explain: A bottle has a cap and a neck, and you pour from it.

text: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
explain: M appears once in minute, twice in moment, and not at all in thousand years.

text: The more of me you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
explain: Each step you take leaves another footstep behind you.

text: What can fill a room yet takes up no space?
explain: Light fills a room but has no size to push other things out.

text: What goes up every year but never comes back down?
explain: Your age rises each year and never goes back down.

text: I have a bed but never sleep, a mouth but never eat, and I run but never walk.
explain: A river has a bed and a mouth, and it runs to the sea.

text: What has teeth but cannot bite, and tidies your hair?
explain: A comb has teeth, cannot bite, and tidies hair. A saw or shark would not.

text: I have one eye but cannot see. You thread me when you sew.
explain: A needle has an eye, the hole you thread when sewing.

text: What can you catch but never throw?
explain: You can catch a cold, but you cannot throw one. Fish and balls can be thrown.

text: What is broken the moment you speak its name?
explain: Saying the word silence out loud ends the silence.

text: What is always ahead of you, yet you can never see it?
explain: The future is always ahead of you and has not happened yet, so it cannot be seen.

text: I am light as a feather, yet no one can hold me for long. What am I?
explain: Breath weighs almost nothing, yet you cannot hold it for long.

text: Four legs at dawn, two at noon, three at dusk, over one life. What am I?
explain: A baby crawls, an adult walks on two legs, and an elder uses a cane.

text: I am tall when young, short when old, and I give light. What am I?
explain: A candle shrinks as it burns and gives light. A pencil or tree does not.

text: What gets bigger the more you take away from it?
explain: Digging out earth makes a hole bigger.

text: I have a thumb and four fingers, but I am not alive. I keep hands warm.
explain: A glove has a thumb and four fingers and keeps hands warm.

text: What runs all around a yard without ever moving?
explain: A fence runs around the yard but stays in place.

text: What belongs to you, yet other people use it more than you do?
explain: Other people say your name far more often than you do.

text: I am full of holes, yet I hold water. What am I?
explain: A sponge is full of holes and soaks up water. A net lets it all through.

text: What has words but never speaks?
explain: A book is full of words but never speaks. A parrot and a radio do.

text: I begin with T, end with T, and am full of tea. What am I?
explain: Teapot begins and ends with T and is full of tea.

text: I travel the world yet stay stuck in one corner. What am I?
explain: A stamp sits in the corner of an envelope while the letter travels.

text: Ann is older than Ben. Ben is older than Cy. Who is the youngest?
explain: Ann > Ben > Cy in age, so Cy is the youngest.

text: Three chairs in a row: green is left of red, red is left of blue. Who is in the middle?
explain: The order is green, red, blue, so red is in the middle.

text: All cats in my house sleep. Milo is a cat in my house. Does Milo sleep?
explain: Every cat in the house sleeps and Milo is one of them.

text: Tom is twice as old as Sue. Sue is 6. How old is Tom?
explain: Twice 6 is 12.

text: Three coins, one heavier. Coin 1 balances Coin 2 on a scale. Which coin is heavier?
explain: If 1 and 2 balance, they weigh the same, so the heavy one is Coin 3.

text: Sam has 3 more marbles than Lia. Together they have 13. How many has Sam?
explain: Lia has 5 and Sam has 8: 5 + 8 = 13 and 8 is 3 more than 5.

text: Ana is taller than Bo. Cy is shorter than Bo. Who is tallest?
explain: Ana > Bo > Cy in height, so Ana is the tallest.

text: In a race Dee beat Eli, Eli beat Fay, and Gus beat Dee. Who came second?
explain: The finish order is Gus, Dee, Eli, Fay, so Dee was second.

text: One prize, three labels. A: “Prize here.” B: “Not here.” C: “Not in A.” Only one is true. Where is it?
explain: In A, labels A and B are true; in C, B and C are true. In B, only C is true.

text: Today is Wednesday. What day was it three days before tomorrow?
explain: Tomorrow is Thursday. Three days before Thursday is Monday.

text: A pen and a notebook cost $11. The notebook costs $10 more than the pen. What does the pen cost?
explain: Pen 50 cents, notebook $10.50: they total $11 and differ by $10.

text: A snail climbs 3 m each day and slips 2 m each night. The wall is 5 m. On which day is it out?
explain: It is at 3 m, then 1 m, then 4 m, then 2 m, and on day 3 it climbs to 5 m.

text: All bloops are razzies. All razzies are lazzies. Are all bloops lazzies?
explain: A bloop is a razzy, and a razzy is a lazzy, so a bloop is a lazzy.

text: Cara has twice as many stickers as Dan. Together they have 18. How many has Dan?
explain: Dan has 6 and Cara has 12: 6 + 12 = 18.

text: A train leaves at 2:15 and the trip takes 1 hour 50 minutes. When does it arrive?
explain: 2:15 plus 1 hour is 3:15, plus 50 minutes is 4:05.

text: Pat is younger than Quin. Rae is older than Quin. Who is in the middle by age?
explain: Pat is youngest, then Quin, then Rae, so Quin is in the middle.

text: Ben, Cal and Dot each have a cat, dog or fish. Ben's has no fur; Cal's barks. Who has the cat?
explain: Ben has the fish and Cal has the dog, so Dot has the cat.

text: A bus has 12 people. 5 get off and 3 get on, then 4 get off. How many are on it?
Bag A weighs the same as B. C is heavier than A. D is lighter than B. Which is heaviest?
explain: A = B, C is above them, and D is below B, so C is heaviest.

text: Ann has twice as many apples as Bo, and Bo twice as many as Cy. They have 14. How many has Ann?
explain: Cy 2, Bo 4, Ann 8 makes 14.

text: A fence has 10 posts in a straight line. How many gaps are between the posts?
explain: Each gap sits between two neighbours, so 10 posts make 9 gaps.

text: Two mothers and two daughters share 3 cakes, one each. How many people are there?
explain: A grandmother, her daughter and her granddaughter: 2 mothers and 2 daughters.

text: Today is Friday. What day is it 100 days from now?
explain: 98 days is 14 whole weeks, back to Friday. Two more days gives Sunday.

text: Three whole numbers in a row add up to 24. What is the smallest?
explain: 7 + 8 + 9 = 24, so the smallest is 7.

text: How many straight cuts turn one rope into 4 pieces?
explain: Each cut adds one piece: 1 cut gives 2, 2 give 3, and 3 give 4.
Each gap grows by 2: +4, +6, +8, so 20 + 10 = 30.
Each number doubles, so 16 x 2 = 32.
Each number doubles, so 40 x 2 = 80.
Each number is the sum of the two before it: 5 + 8 = 13.
These are square numbers: 1x1, 2x2 ... 5x5, so next is 6x6 = 36.
Each step subtracts 9: 73 - 9 = 64.

text: A, C, E, G, ?
explain: Skip one letter each time, so after G (skipping H) comes I.

text: Z, X, V, T, ?
explain: Go backwards, skipping one letter each time: after T (skipping S) comes R.
These are the prime numbers in order. The next prime after 11 is 13.
Each number is divided by 3, so 3 / 3 = 1.
Double and add 1 each time: 15 x 2 + 1 = 31.

text: First letters of the months: J, F, M, A, M, ?
explain: January, February, March, April, May, then June.

text: First letters of One, Two, Three and so on: O, T, T, F, F, S, S, ?
explain: After Seven comes Eight, which starts with E.
Double and add 1 each time: 23 x 2 + 1 = 47.
Multiply by 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6: 120 x 6 = 720.
The gaps are 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9: 19 + 9 = 28.

text: B, D, G, K, ?
explain: The letters jump by 2, 3, 4, then 5: K (11th) + 5 = P (16th).
These are cubes: 1x1x1, 2x2x2, 3x3x3, 4x4x4. Next is 5x5x5 = 125.
The rule alternates +2, -1, +2, -1, so 7 + 2 = 9.
The gaps double: +2, +4, +8, then +16, so 17 + 16 = 33.

text: AB, BC, CD, ?
explain: Each pair moves one letter forward in the alphabet: after CD comes DE.
The letter steps back one and the number goes up one: W4.
The gaps grow by 2: +2, +4, +6, then +8, so 14 + 8 = 22.
The gaps are 1, 2, 3, 4, so the next gap is 5: 10 + 5 = 15.
The gaps are 1, 2, 3, 4, so the next gap is 5: 11 + 5 = 16.

text: Which word uses exactly the letters of EARTH?
explain: Heart has the same five letters as EARTH in a new order.

text: Which word uses exactly the letters of STOP?
explain: Pots is STOP with the letters rearranged. Spit has an I, and Stoop has an extra O.

text: Change one letter of CAT to get a flying night-time animal.
explain: Changing C to B gives bat, an animal that flies at night.

text: Which word hides a body part?
explain: Charm hides ARM.

text: Which is the odd one out?
explain: Apple and plum are fruits; a carrot is a vegetable.

text: Which is the odd one out?
explain: Red and green are colours; tall is not.

text: Which is the odd one out?
explain: A flute and a harp are musical instruments; a chair is furniture.

text: Which is the odd one out?
explain: Rose and tulip are flowers; a maple is a tree.

text: Which is the odd one out?
explain: Mars and Venus are planets; the Moon is not.

text: Change one letter of HOT to get something you wear on your head.
explain: Changing O to A gives hat. A hut is a small house.

text: Which word reads the same forwards and backwards?
explain: Level is spelled L-E-V-E-L in both directions.

text: Which word spells another word when read backwards?
explain: Draw backwards is ward. Plane and sheep give nonsense.

text: Which word hides a colour?
explain: Credit hides RED.

text: Which word hides an animal?
explain: Scatter hides CAT.

text: Add one letter to FAR to make a place where crops grow.
explain: FAR plus M is farm, where crops grow.

text: Which word has its letters in alphabetical order?
explain: A, L, M, O, S, T go in alphabet order. Spoon and tree do not.

text: Which word contains all five vowels: A, E, I, O and U?
explain: Education has e, u, a, i and o. Question has no A.

text: Which is the odd one out?
explain: Hour and minute measure time; a meter measures length.

text: Which word uses exactly the letters of RACE?
explain: Care has the same four letters as RACE. Cart and core change a letter.

text: Remove the first letter of BEAT to get something you do at a meal.
explain: BEAT without its first letter is EAT.

text: Which is the odd one out?
explain: Quick and rapid mean fast; slow means the opposite.

text: Rearrange the letters of NEVES to make a number.
explain: NEVES rearranged is SEVEN.

text: Which word rhymes with BLUE?
explain: Shoe and blue end in the same sound.

text: Which word sounds the same as KNIGHT?
explain: Knight and night sound alike but are spelled differently.

text: Which word has RAT hidden inside?
explain: Pirate hides RAT: pi-RAT-e.
